detail.longDescription: Hey HN, I'm Fabio, the creator of Beolis. I've built Beolis ( https://beolis.com ) to better handle coding on agentic scenarios. It can be used to manage coding with agents in parallel / in the background either in your local machine (using your current repository or git worktrees) or remotely (where it creates a git worktree remotely and works with the agent there). Although it uses agents you don't need to "chat" with the agent at each step as you usually do when dealing with agents (although you still can), but rather create workflows where you can code the default steps you want. This means that instead of saying 'run the tests' to an agent the idea is that you (or the agent) create code that will actually run the tests and then if it fails it goes to a cheap agent to summarize the failures and then onto a smarter agent to actually do the fixes and work on the problems found -- I find my tokens last much longer given that approach ;) I've been using Beolis to build itself (started back in February) and I believe it's now stable for day-to-day use. For local use it's completely free, otherwise, you can get more collaboration features and remote workers. I'd love to hear feedback.
